summary:
Salt & Onion Pepper Shrimp Creamy Mushroom Pasta

Ingredients
- Shrimp — peeled and deveined
- Mushrooms — sliced
- Onion — diced
- Pasta
- Cream (or milk/cream cheese for a lighter sauce)
- Salt & pepper — generous, to taste
- Garlic — minced (optional)
- Butter or oil — for cooking
- Parmesan — optional, for finishing

Method
1. Cook pasta in salted boiling water
2. Season shrimp with salt and pepper. Sear in butter/oil until just pink; remove and set aside.
3. In the same pan, sauté onion until soft and translucent, then add garlic and mushrooms; cook until golden and softened.
4. Pour in cream (or milk/cream cheese), simmer briefly, and season with salt and pepper.
5. Add pasta and shrimp, toss to coat; loosen with pasta water if needed.
6. Finish with parmesan and extra black pepper.

Notes / Reflections
- The onion adds a sweet base layer before the mushrooms so it releases sweetness into the sauce.
- Mushrooms need a hot pan and patience to brown — don't crowd them.
- you can swap cream for cream cheese if you have extra on hand.
YUMMMM！

summary:
Cranberry Cream Cheese Cookies (Air Fryer)

Ingredients
- Cream cheese – (main base for me touse up your stash! you don't have to!)
- Flour – enough to bring the dough together
- Dried cranberries – they provide most of the sweetness
- Sugar – just a littleeeeeeee
- Butter – a small amount

Method
1. Mix cream cheese, a little butter, and a little sugar until smooth.
2. Add flour and dried cranberries; mix into a dough.
3. Shape into a square block.
4. Freeze until firm.
5. Slice thin.
6. Air fry at 160°C for 10 minutes.

Notes / Reflections
- Using cream cheese as the main fat instead of butter also works well and is a good way to use up extra cream cheese!
- The cranberries carry most of the sweetness, so only a little added sugar is needed just in case
- Freezing the dough makes thin, even slices easy.
- Thin slices cook fast in the air fryer - 160°C for 10 minutes was just right for me since I cut them each very thin
- Overall: a simple, less-buttery twist on classic cranberry cookies, and a nice way to clear out the cream cheese(healthier than using butter!)

summary:
Apple Pie with Lattice Top

Ingredients

For the crust:
- Flour
- Cold butter (cubed)
- milk
- Pinch of salt
butter

For the filling:
- Apples — peeled, cored, sliced
- honey — to taste
- Lemon juice (optional, to keep apples from browning)
- A little flour or cornstarch (to thicken juices)
- Butter — a few small pieces

For finishing:
- Egg wash (egg + a splash of water)

Method
1. Make the crust: cut cold butter into flour and salt until crumbly; add milk gradually until the dough just comes together. Split into two discs, wrap, and chill.
2. Make the filling: toss sliced apples with sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice, and flour/cornstarch.
3. Roll out the first disc and fit into the pie dish; add the apple filling and dot with butter.
4. Roll out the second disc and cut into even strips.
5. Weave a lattice: lay strips one direction, then weave the cross strips over-and-under alternately. Trim and crimp the edges.
6. Brush the lattice with egg wash and sprinkle with coarse sugar.
7. Bake until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles ( 180°C, 20 mins, cover the edges with foil if they brown too fast).
8. Cool before slicing so the filling sets.

Notes / Reflections.
- Slice apples evenly so they cook at the same rate.
- Don't overfill; too much filling makes the lattice sink and the pie soggy.
- Weave the lattice loosely as the strips shrink a bit as they bake.
- Let it cool, cutting too early makes the filling run.
ENJOY!!!!my mom loves it!

summary:
Cranberry-Filled Boat-Shaped Cakes

Ingredients
- Flour, butter (or cream cheese), sugar, eggs, milk, baking powder, pinch of salt
- Dried cranberries with water/juice (simmered into a thick filling)

Method
1. Simmer cranberries with sugar and a splash of water until thick; cool.
2. Cream butter/cream cheese with sugar, add eggs, then fold in flour, baking powder, salt, and milk until smooth.
3. Fill boat molds halfway, add cranberry filling, cover with more batter.
4. Bake at ~180°C until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

Notes
- The filling and sweetness balanced well, but the dough came out a bit too thick and hard — next time I'd make the batter thinner/softer and keep the layer of dough thinner so the filling shines more.
- Keep the filling thick so it doesn't sink.
- Fill molds only halfway so they don't overflow.
black sesames made it looking more delicious!:)
